units.translation: For Sophocles seems to use it (τὴν πέμφιγα [the blast]) of breath, but Aeschylus in Prometheus Bound (or rather in Prometheus Unbound, fr. 195): εὐθεῖαν ἕρπε τήνδε [go straight on this way]; and first you will come to the blasts of the North Wind, where beware the roaring storm, lest it suddenly snatch you up, whirling you with its wintry blast. And Sophocles seems to use the word πέμφιξ [blast] of the rays themselves, and so does Aeschylus in the Wool-Carders (fr. 169): ἃς οὔτε πέμφιξ ἡλίου προσδέρκεται οὔτ᾽ ἀστερωπὸν ὄμμα Λητῴας κόρης [whom neither the sun's ray looks upon nor the starry eye of Leto's daughter]. And of a drop the same poet says in Prometheus (fr. 195): ἐξευλαβοῦ δὲ μή σε προσβάλη στόμα πέμφιξ [beware lest a drop strike your mouth]; for it is bitter, and its vapors are not life-giving. And in Pentheus (fr. 182): μηδ᾽ αἵματος πέμφιγα πρὸς πέδῳ βάλης [do not cast a drop of blood upon the ground].
πέμφιξ [blast]. Breath. Aeschylus in the Wool-Carders, of the rays.
grief, steadfast of heart, is fitting for each house
Pentheus, son of Echion and Agave, king of Thebes.
Pentheus was the title of a tragedy by Aeschylus (fr. 182).
having sewn up a fate for Pentheus
which Eustathius p. 415, 7 interprets as, ὦ τράγε, πάνυ στερήσῃ γενείου, εἰ τὴν φλόγα φιλήσεις [O goat, you will be utterly deprived of your beard, if you love the flame].
the house mourns the man, bereaved
Why must we mourn these things?
for enemies are those whom it befits to mourn with hair
he mourns a new grief for the young
goat, you will surely mourn your beard
O goat, you will be utterly deprived of your beard, if you love the flame
without mourning rites you endured to bury the man unlamented
dream-apparitions, mournful, are present as phantoms
you indeed will cause many mourners
of the city's race, a mourner
a lock for Inachus, a nurture-offering, and this second one, a mourning-offering
and from tears drips a mournful reverence
the city of Susa and of Ecbatana you hid in dark grief
I think my sister is walking, conspicuous in baneful grief
hear now, father, in turn, my many-teared griefs
